newsitem.title: USA: Police offer massive reward in Florida robbery.
newsitem.headline: Police offer massive reward in Florida robbery.

text.p: Florida police and the FBI offered a massive half-million dollar reward Friday for information leading to the arrest of a suspect in the theft of funds from security firm Loomis Fargo in Jacksonville.
Although the amount stolen was not revealed, the size of the reward suggested it was considerable.
Unconfirmed media reports put the haul at up to $20 million, which would make the theft one of the biggest in U.S. history.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Jacksonville Sheriff's Office, in a joint statement, said they were seeking Philip Noel Johnson, 37, as a possible suspect in the robbery, which took place March 29, and in the kidnapping of two fellow employees at Loomis Fargo.
Johnson should be considered "armed and dangerous," police said.
It gave no details of how the robbery was carried out.
Johnson was last seen driving a white van with Florida license plates, which was recovered in Asheville, North Carolina, March 31, the statement said.
The $500,000 reward was for "the arrest and conviction of the person or persons responsible for the robbery of Loomis Fargo and recovery of the stolen funds," the statement said.
Loomis Fargo was formed in 1996 from the merger of armoured transport firms Loomis Armoured Inc and Wells Fargo Armoured Service.
